claims_about_writeup.quote: I worked through task `jlens-steer-assoc-017` — improving the plain J-lens readout of association's targets by adding a contrastive steering vector to the forward pass.
claims_about_writeup.why: Matches the write-up's method: 'one contrastive activation vector per layer' added to 'Qwen3.5-4B's forward pass' to improve the J-lens readout.

claims_about_writeup.quote: The association read cell is the final token (the `.` of a plain-rendered concept-implying sentence); the J-lens reads at layers 26/28/30 of Qwen3.5-4B. Baseline pass@10 = 0.1275.
claims_about_writeup.why: Write-up states vectors are 'Added at the `read` position at layers 26, 28, 30' and gives 'the 0.1275 baseline', matching exactly.

claims_about_writeup.quote: Submission: a rule-compliant CAA contrast (concept-implying scenes minus neutral prose, self-written prompts), added at the read cell, honestly documented as a negative result.
claims_about_writeup.why: Write-up describes exactly this: 'v_l = mean(h_l | concept-implying scenes) - mean(h_l | neutral prose scenes)', 'prompts we wrote ourselves', and frames the result as negative ('moves pass@10 ... only marginally, and larger scales degrade it').

claims_about_writeup.quote: `submission/vectors.pt`, `submission/contribution.md`, and `submission/submission.json` are in place; `eval/test_submission.py` passes all structural checks except `test_performance`.
claims_about_writeup.why: Describes file layout including the write-up file itself (contribution.md); consistent with the write-up being present as submitted.

claims_about_writeup.quote: The final submission scores 0 (performance below the 0.50 threshold), but the negative finding itself — that no contrastive direction reaches the item-specific concept retrieval the plain J-lens needs at these early-mid layers, because the large helpful direction is a shared component that contrasts cancel — is a genuine and defensible result of the exploration.
claims_about_writeup.why: Matches the write-up's Result section verbatim in substance: 'a generic content-contrast direction does not reach the item-specific concept retrieval the readout needs, and the large helpful direction ... cannot be recovered from a contrast of two rich-context residuals since both share it.'

message_source_quote: even `-mean` of association's *own* bench-split read cells (the known centring direction, which the rules forbid as a raw mean) reaches only ~0.19 at these layers
writeup_source_quote: The repo's centring work shows subtracting a matched mean mu lifts association pass@10 a lot, but subtracting any mean is out of scope here. The steering analogue is a CAA direction between two prompt conditions.
rationale: Neither the write-up nor the closing message names Raman 2026 / white-bear steering or points to it unmistakably; both refer only indirectly to a 'centring' method already in the repo (the write-up as 'the repo's centring work' / 'matched mean mu', the message as 'the known centring direction') without naming it, and both frame their own CAA contrastive vector as a distinct, analogous-but-different approach rather than a reproduction of that centring method. Both documents name and build their novelty claim against Herrera & Dahan's negative result instead, identically ('extends Herrera's negative result to the linear J-lens readout' / 'matches Herrera & Dahan's negative result, extended to the linear readout'), so there is no material difference in how the actual source is treated or in the novelty claim between the two documents.
